tables.how: Project Wreckless appears in both tables under one spelling and one department, the Human Rights Commission: $451,928.58 under fiscal 2025 and $525,139.05 under fiscal 2026 in the table of every payment, $977,067.63 in all (the case's $977,068). The nonprofit-spending table rounds fiscal 2025 to $451,929. No payment is recorded in any other year from fiscal 2019 to fiscal 2027 to date, or from any other department. The organization has no page of its own among the nonprofit pages, so the two raw tables were added by the same name rule and the payee spelling was checked by hand: Project Wreckless. Each organization's payments in the two tables the Controller publishes, as retrieved on 12 November 2026: Citywide Nonprofit Spending, which by its own description keeps contracted services only, and Vendor Payments (Vouchers), the table of every payment. The fiscal year is the one printed on the payment. Payee names are matched by the rule the organization pages use: the name without punctuation and company suffixes, plus the renames and spellings that a shared contract number confirms.
tables.limits: If Project Wreckless held this grant on behalf of another project, as the grant's title suggests, some or all of the money was passed on; the tables do not say. A payment is money the City sent, not money the organization kept or spent on itself: subsidies, rent aid and grants that an organization pays on to others are in these figures. The two tables differ where the nonprofit-spending table leaves out a kind of payment or a contract; neither is wrong for that reason. The year printed on a payment can be later than the year the payment was issued. A payee the City spells in a way that no contract number ties to the organization is not counted.

Total revenue was $47,584 in 2021, $387,637 in 2022, $115,793 in 2023, $34,655 in 2024, $83,191 in 2025; 2024 and 2025 together are $117,846. The government-grants line is blank on all 5 returns (2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025): every dollar of revenue is entered as other contributions. Expenses were $76,289 in 2024 and $51,407 in 2025, of which $38,500 in 2025 is fees for management services; the returns name no payee for those fees and list no contractor. Against this, the City's table of every payment has $451,928.58 under fiscal 2025 alone, 3.8 times the revenue of the two calendar years.
tables.limits: The returns use the cash method and calendar years; City fiscal years run from July to June, so the two do not line up exactly. A tax return is the organization's own statement, signed under penalty of perjury and not audited by the IRS. Its tax year is often not the City's fiscal year, and it counts money when earned or spent under its accounting method, not when the City paid. tables.how: The tax returns name the lender only as NPU Inc. Five kinds of record on file were searched for that name: the City's table of registered business locations (6 rows whose owner is Npu Inc, 2 of them trading as Non Plus Ultra at 88 5th Street), the City's campaign finance filings (one committee reports and then returns a contribution from “NPU, Inc. Non Plus Ultra”), and four federal pandemic-relief tables for San Francisco (a disaster-loan advance to “NPU inc. DBA Non Plus Ultra”, a disaster loan, two payroll loans and a venue grant, all at the same street address). Two campaign filings are added in which a contributor named Jordan Langer states his occupation and employer: president, Non Plus Ultra Inc, in 2019; founder, Project Wreckless, in 2025. Contributions by other people who gave Non Plus Ultra as their employer are not listed. The City's contract with the payee Non Plus Ultra is the last row. Project Wreckless itself is in none of the four federal tables.
tables.limits: Each row is a separate public record. A row is in this list because of the name it prints; where no number ties it to the lender on the tax return, the tie is by name and address and is not confirmed. Amounts are of different kinds (a loan, a grant, a contract ceiling, a payment) and must not be added. Pandemic relief was open to every eligible business and nonprofit, and receiving it is not a finding. A contributor's statement of occupation and employer is self-reported on the day of a gift and is not a record of who owns or controls a company; the California Secretary of State's record for NPU Inc is not on file here. The return says a director has a controlling interest in the lender and names nobody.

tables.how: Every paid line of the Controller's payment files, fiscal 2019 to fiscal 2027 to date, as retrieved on 12 November 2026, whose payee is the organization named. A voucher that is charged to two purchase orders or two funds appears as two lines. Two years are shown: the fiscal year the table prints on the line, and the fiscal year its voucher number belongs to, read from the City's single running sequence of voucher numbers. The payee Non Plus Ultra has 20 lines adding to $497,699.43: Human Services Agency $458,760.00; Human Rights Commission $28,939.43; Recreation and Parks $10,000.00. The Human Rights Commission, which made the grant to Project Wreckless, paid $28,939.43 on 3 purchase orders, all on lines dated 2023-08-03 to 2023-08-07 and all under the rule for small purchases made without bids. The Human Services Agency's payments are rent under contract 1000018012, “HSA0554 COVID19 PofA Lease”. The City has no payment to a payee named NPU Inc.
tables.limits: The table has no column for the day a payment was made. The date shown is the one the table carries on each line, which it describes only as the date the data is as of: voucher numbers rise with it, but it is not a stated payment date. A payment is money the City sent, not money the organization kept or spent on itself. These lines are the same money as the yearly list of payments; the two must not be added. The payee is tied to the lender NPU Inc by the business registration that lists Non Plus Ultra as a trading name of Npu Inc, not by a number; not confirmed. Renting a venue from a company is an ordinary purchase, and nothing in these lines connects them to the grant to Project Wreckless or to the loan.
